riskReasons: The accepted name and supported taxon are consistent across the reviewed institutional sources.
Seasonal colour descriptions are compatible but intensity and timing remain site-dependent.
No material synonym, commercial-renaming or core-morphology conflict was found.

duplicateCheck.notes: Compared with all Reference Standards RC-001–RC-010 and all other owner-approved Catalogue assignments CUL-000012–CUL-000025. It is distinct from RC-009 ‘Katsura’ by its governed seasonal sequence and from RC-005 ‘Aureum’ by taxon, leaf expression and overall profile. No probable duplicate remains.

identityNotes: The accepted working name follows the RHS accepted plant profile and the approved identity registry. No synonym is approved. The profile describes a named cultivar but does not authenticate individual plants from colour or habit alone.

content.summary: A medium-sized, bushy Japanese maple selected for a bright seasonal sequence: yellow to yellow-orange spring foliage, greener summer leaves and orange-yellow autumn colour, with bright green bark adding secondary interest.
content.habit: Bushy, rounded deciduous shrub or small tree, commonly described around 3 m in garden conditions; architecture and final scale depend on age, site, training and rootstock.
content.leafForm: Palmate leaves in the ordinary palmatum horticultural group rather than a dissected or linearilobum form; the principal Catalogue value is seasonal colour rather than a uniquely diagnostic leaf outline.

seasonal.spring: Leaves open yellow, with an orange to orange-red edge reported by NC State; exact saturation varies with exposure and observation date.
seasonal.summer: Foliage becomes greenish to lime green rather than remaining uniformly yellow.
seasonal.autumn: Leaves turn orange-yellow, sometimes with stronger orange expression under favourable seasonal conditions.

size.qualifier: RHS published range with a stated 10–20-year time to maturity; use as an approximate garden range, not a fixed maximum.

content.cultivation: Grow in moist but well-drained soil in a sheltered position, in full sun to partial shade. Reliable moisture and protection from excessive exposure reduce scorch risk; partial shade is useful where summers are hot or drying.
content.diagnostic: Compare with RC-009 ‘Katsura’, whose spring-emergence profile is a different chartreuse and yellow-orange trajectory, and with RC-005 ‘Aureum’, which belongs to Acer shirasawanum and has a different leaf and taxon profile. Colour resemblance alone does not authenticate ‘Orange Dream’.
content.confidence: High confidence in the accepted name, taxon and broad seasonal sequence; moderate confidence in exact colour intensity and mature dimensions because these vary by source framework, site and age.
content.unresolvedIssue: The lean review did not establish a primary origin history or quantify how consistently the orange-red spring margin appears across climates; neither gap creates a material identity conflict.
